cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster, and he's talking straight to the LORD. He opens with, "O LORD, You have searched me and known me." Friend, I got searched every single time somebody dug through my junk drawer looking for tape, but NOBODY ever knew me.

cards.question: David says the LORD knows when he sits down and when he gets up. What else does the LORD understand from afar?

cards.text: The LORD searches out David's path and his lying down, and He's aware of ALL his ways. ALL of them, friend, and some days I'm not even aware of all MY ways.

cards.question: David says the LORD only knows his words after he says them out loud.

cards.text: Then David says the LORD hems him in behind and before, and has laid His hand on him. Behind AND before, friend, so David can't even back out of this one.

cards.question: The LORD knows David inside and out, and David says knowledge like that is too lofty for him to attain. What does he mean?

answers.text: He can't fully take it in

cards.text: Then David asks two questions: "Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence?" Buckle up, friend, because he's about to picture every hiding spot there is.

cards.question: David says that if he went up to the heavens or made his bed in Sheol, the realm of the dead, the LORD would be there too.

cards.text: Next he pictures rising on the wings of the dawn, or settling by the farthest sea. Friend, that's the "new phone number, no forwarding address" plan, and every adult has thought about it at least once.

cards.question: Even by the farthest sea, David says the LORD's right hand will hold him fast.

cards.text: Last idea: what if David says the darkness will surely hide him, and the light around him will become night? Friend, that's porch light off, curtains shut, pretending NOBODY'S home.

cards.question: Why can't the darkness hide David from God?

answers.text: Night is as bright as day to God
God simply waits for the morning
David's voice always gives him away

cards.text: Now David goes back before he was even born: the LORD formed his inmost being and knit him together in his mother's womb. KNIT him, friend, and I still need three tries to tie my own apron.

cards.question: Thinking about how God made him, what does David do?

cards.text: David says he is fearfully and wonderfully made, and he knows very well that God's works are marvelous. Friend, I once sold for 25 cents out of a clearance bin, and even I'm feeling that one.

cards.question: David was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth. He says his frame was hidden from God while he was being made.

cards.text: And God's eyes saw David's body while it was still unformed. Not finished, not even close, and God was already looking.

cards.question: David says all his days were written in God's book only after he lived them.

cards.text: I think David is in awe here. He tells God that His thoughts are precious to him.

cards.question: David compares God's thoughts to the grains of sand. He's saying God's thoughts are too ___ to count.

cards.text: Then David says, "…when I awake, I am still with You." Most folks wake up and slap the snooze button, but David wakes up and he's STILL with God.
Then the psalm takes a hard turn. David turns his attention to the wicked.

cards.question: What does David ask God to do to the wicked?
David tells the bloodthirsty men to get away from him. He says they speak of God with honest words.

cards.text: David asks, "Do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD, and detest those who rise against You?" Then he says he hates them with perfect hatred and counts them as his enemies.

Then David circles back to how this psalm opened, and now he's ASKING for it: "Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns." Most folks dodge the checkup, but David is BOOKING one.

cards.question: David asks God to see if there's any offensive way in him.
David's last request is to be led somewhere. Where?

answers.text: In the way that lasts forever
In the way of his fathers
In the way back to Jerusalem
